newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iraq in production-sharing deal with China - MEES.
newsitem.headline: Iraq in production-sharing deal with China - MEES.

text.p: Iraq and China have initialed a production-sharing deal to develop the al-Ahdab oilfield in central Iraq, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) reported on Monday.

MEES said the agreement was signed two months ago by the Iraqi oil minister and senior officials of the China National Petroleum Corp (CNPC) and will become effective when it receives final approval from Iraqi President Saddam Hussein.
The field's production capacity is preliminarily put at about 80,000 barrels per day (bpd), MEES said.
"This is the first agreement to be initialed by the Iraqi oil authorities, who have been carrying out upstream talks with foreign firms during the past five years," MEES said.

"...The fact that the Ministry of Oil has decided to propose a production-sharing agreement to the political authorities is a significant breakthrough in the prolonged negotiations with foreign firms and is an important challenge to the U.N. sanctions regime," it added.
China, faced with ever-growing energy demand, was in August holding discussions with isolated Iraq to co-operate in seismic studies and exploration in Iraqi oilfields.
"The Iraqi oil authorities have held upstream talks with over a score of European, Asian, Arab and even some U.S. firms, but no agreements have been concluded yet," said MEES.
Iraq signed a $2 billion oil-for-food deal with the United Nations in May but it was delayed following Saddam's foray into northern Iraq in August.
